question: A wood boring shipworm is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**teredo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Teredo** is a genus of wood-boring bivalve mollusks, commonly known as shipworms.
 
• Shipworms, including those from the genus Teredo, are notorious for boring into and damaging wooden structures submerged in seawater, such as ships, piers, and docks.
 
• Teredo species have elongated, worm-like bodies and shell-like valves at their anterior end which they use to bore into wood.
 
• They are capable of digesting cellulose in wood, thanks to symbiotic bacteria present in their gills that help them break down the wood fibers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Umax**

 
 
• Umax is not related to wood-boring organisms. It is often associated with imaging products and technology, such as scanners and printers.
 
 
 
• **Patella**
 
 
• Patella refers to a genus of marine gastropod mollusks known as limpets. They are not wood-boring and are commonly found attached to rocks in the intertidal zone.
 
 
 
• **Chiton**
 
 
• Chitons are marine mollusks belonging to the class Polyplacophora. They have a distinctive eight-plated shell and are found on rocky shores but are not known for boring into wood.
